newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slipped back on Tuesday in a relatively calm session where no one issue provided direction but a combination of potentially negative factors weighed on sentiment, trader said.

After a positive opening the contract drifted off the highs with Bunds and was then hit by some large sell orders late in the session. Traders said it smacked of book closing ahead of the year end rather than the taking of new short positions.
The traders said day traders helped stabilise the contract going into the close by buying back short positions they had put on earlier in the day.

"There was no really big news, people were playing the zone 128.60 to 129.00. The selling was more lightening or getting out of positions before the end of the year," said a trader at a French brokerage.

He said people were talking about apparent differences between France and Germany both over the stability pact and also the notion of an independent European central bank following President Jacques Chirac's statement on Monday that it should be counterbalanced by a political power.
"Chirac made a tactical mistake. It's not a description of independence they're familiar with in Frankfurt," said a trader.
Another trader at a French brokerage said the direction of the market late in the session was "provided by a very big seller, a non-resident fund closing out positions."
Several traders said a successful conclusion to the stability pact negotiations in Dublin later this week was looking more remote and that the added uncertainty was a slightly negative factor.
The franc weakness which traders again attributed to several contributary factors, also weighed slightly on the market, especially at the short end, traders said.
A trader said he thought caution ahead of Chirac's television interview scheduled for Thursday evening was one reason for some franc weakness. "I wouldn't buy the market ahead of Chirac," he said.
The franc slipped as low as 3.3838 against the mark from 3.3772 late on Monday and was trading at 3.3822 at 1700 GMT.
The Treasury announced it would be selling 300 to 500 million Ecu of its five- and 10-year benchmark bonds on Thursday at a regular monthly auction.
